text: On 23 November 2026 the wind fleet generated an average of 6892 MW, with a minimum of 4031 MW and a maximum of 11507 MW. Over the previous seven‑day window the mean was 7963 MW, so output was 13.4% lower. Forty‑seven wind periods were recorded out of the 48 periods expected, with one missing period each for wind_offshore and wind_onshore. System demand averaged 35034 MW and peaked at 43134 MW, 7.1% higher than the prior week’s mean of 32701 MW. The average electricity price was £195.9/​MWh, ranging from £154.6/​MWh to £251.2/​MWh, which is 5.2% higher than the previous seven‑day mean of £186.1/​MWh. Day‑ahead forecasts performed well: wind forecast MAE was 1231 MW versus a baseline MAE of 6104 MW, and demand forecast MAE was 1072 MW against a baseline of 1603 MW, with a demand MAPE of 2.94%. Data‑quality checks covered 29 series, with 25 passing, 2 warnings and 2 failures; the failures were wind_onshore and wind_offshore, and the warnings related to price_apx and price_n2ex.
